html:
The Battle of Nahavand was fought in 642 near the town of Nahavand in the Zagros mountains of western Iran. An Arab Muslim army defeated the last great army of the Sasanian Empire.

After losing Iraq at al-Qadisiyyah, King Yazdegerd III gathered a large force. The Arabs, sent by the caliph Umar, lured it out of its fortified camp with a pretended retreat and routed it. Arab writers called it the victory of victories.

After Nahavand the Sasanian state fell apart province by province. Yazdegerd fled east and was killed near Merv in 651. Iran became part of the caliphate, and over the next centuries most Iranians became Muslim, while keeping the Persian language. See also the Arab conquests.
sum: The Battle of Nahavand was fought in 642 near the town of Nahavand in the Zagros mountains of western Iran. An Arab Muslim army defeated the last great army of the Sasanian Empire.
